messages:
alice.dev: Heads-up — the canary for dynamic-routing-v2 just started showing elevated 502s and latency spikes. I see a jump from ~0.2% to ~6% error rate across the canary pool. Not safe to continue rolling.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2026-03-15T14:12Z for dynamic-routing-v2 started. 10% traffic -> 4 pods. Health checks passing initially.
incidents-bot: ALERT: 502 rate > 5% in service:redwood-router (canary). Threshold breached for 2 consecutive 1m windows. Paging oncall-sre.
oncall-sre: on it. Pulling logs/metrics now. Can someone confirm whether the automated rollback is supposed to trigger at 5%? I can't find a note in the rollout config quick glance.
alice.dev: It should — policy is sample_threshold=0.05, window=60s. But I think the config that got applied had sample_threshold=0.5 (typo). Looks like a decimal shifted.
maria.eng: Confirmed — I can reproduce 502 locally against the canary. Quick mitigation plan: 1) flip feature flag kill-switch to route back to stable; 2) drain canary pods; 3) rollback artifact from tag dynamic-routing:v2 -> v1.8. I'll take the flag flip.
ops-lead: If we flip the flag, will that be instant for customers? Any cache/edge delay?
maria.eng: Should be near-instant inside the infra. Edge may take up to 30s due to LB sticky sessions. We'll instruct 60s buffer for users.
alice.dev: maria, please run the flag toggle and paste the command/output here.
maria.eng: Running now:

```bash
# internal flagctl CLI
flagctl toggle --flag dynamic-routing-v2 --env prod --value off --reason "canary 502 spike"
```

maria.eng: Output:

```text
INFO flagctl: contacting control-plane
INFO flagctl: flag dynamic-routing-v2 set to OFF for env=prod
OK
```

incidents-bot: ACTION: feature flag dynamic-routing-v2 set to OFF by maria.eng at 2026-03-15T14:15:10Z. Notifying routing service to revert.
oncall-sre: Flipped. I'm seeing traffic shift away from canary now — 4 pods draining. Error rate trending down in the canary pool.
alice.dev: Good. Next, let's prevent the automated rollback logic from misfiring in the future: looks like the decimal was lost in templating. I'll follow up with infra/CI to require explicit decimal formatting in the rollout manifest.
ops-lead: Can someone start a quick verification checklist so we can mark incident status and notify customers if needed?
maria.eng: Verification checklist:
1) Confirm canary 502 rate back to baseline (<0.5%)
2) Confirm global 99th p95 latency within 10% of baseline
3) Re-deploy stable or revert rollout config (depends on root cause)
4) Run smoke test suite against routing in prod (sample 20 requests)
alice.dev: Running smoke test now. curl snippet:

```bash
for i in {1..20}; do curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://api.redwood.example/ping || true; done
```

alice.dev: Results: majority 200s, times ~0.18-0.22s, no 502s in sample.
oncall-sre: Metrics look stable. 502 rate across the cluster down to 0.18% over the last 5m window. p95 latency back to 0.21s (baseline 0.19s). I'll keep an eye for the next 15m.
sam.product: From product side — do we need a customer note? Any requests failed or degraded during the ~3 minute window?
oncall-sre: Based on logs, there were a handful of errors (~300 unique requests) routed during the initial canary window. Most retried clients recovered. No large-scale data loss.
ops-lead: Draft for customers: short apology, mention brief degraded experience for a small subset due to canary routing experiment, mitigation done, monitoring in place. @sam.product can you draft and we can ship.
sam.product: Drafting now, will share soon.
alice.dev: Root cause summary for the incident: rollout manifest template converted 0.05 to 5 due to missing decimal formatting in templating engine; automated rollback thresholds used the value from the manifest so it never triggered. The immediate mitigation was a manual flag kill-switch + draining canary pods.
maria.eng: Action items before close:
- CI: enforce decimal format in rollout templates (owner: infra) [P1]
- Add a secondary automated rollback guard based on absolute 5xx count (owner: runtime) [P2]
- Postmortem with timeline + artifacts (owner: alice.dev) [P1]
oncall-sre: I'll keep monitoring. If error creeps back up we'll re-open and start a full rollback of the artifact to v1.8.
incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident severity set to Sev3. Start postmortem runbook draft at /incidents/2213456789.
sam.product: Customer note ready: "We briefly observed elevated errors for a small number of API requests while a canary rollout was running. We reverted the canary and have confirmed service health; no customer data was impacted. We're investigating root cause and will follow up."
ops-lead: Looks fine, send from status@redwood with incident id 2026-2213456789.
oncall-sre: Confirmed steady state for 20m. Closing paging handoff to monitoring. If anyone sees anomalies, ping this thread and I'll re-activate.
alice.dev: Thanks team. I'll file the postmortem and include the rollout manifest snippets and the flagctl outputs. Closing thread in 1h if no regressions. :thumbsup:
